body.p: Two girls. There once lived two girls. Their mother raised them both. The eldest daughter did not listen to her mother's words. She always demanded good clothes from her mother, good food. The youngest grew silently. She listened to her mother's words, watched her mother sew. The remains of what the mother sewed, she collected, helped the mother to sew. Sweeps, billets, sews. She looked at the maternal seams. She collected pieces. She watched how her mother sews: she examined the seams on their clothes, examined the patterns, the material, what material their things were made of. Then she sits down separately and sews clothes for the doll. These clothes were very beautiful. She herself was small, with a one-span hem and a one-span back, and a cheeky little face like the full moon. And her hand was like a spring on a gun. Her sister was a beauty, like a piece of the sun. Her mouth is scarlet like a lint-free cloth, as if she held a red lint-free cloth in her mouth. But at the same time she was evil. One day their mother died. The children remained in the tent. After the mother died, they themselves began to live. They fished, put nooses on birds, picked berries. So they survived until autumn. The elder sister says: âLet's go to our relatives. Maybe they can help us." The youngest does not want to: âIt's a long way to go there. Our clothes are bad, we won't get there. Let's sew clothes for ourselves." The eldest replies: âWhat will we sew from? There are no paws and no skins. The younger one poured all the shreds that she collected onto the floor. She says: âI used to collect maternal shreds, here they are. Now let's sew some of them. If this is not enough, let's see what we can take from old clothes and add it. The sister wrinkled her face and said: âShall we add something from old clothes? I won't wear this. I'd better go now before the cold sets in. And you stay." She did not listen to her little sister. And she persuaded: "Stay, do not go." "No, I don't want to stay." The youngest was left alone in the tent. From scraps, she began to sew clothes. So beautifully assembled, as if sewn from a single skin. She sewed a coat for herself in a short time, she made shoes and siskins (stockings). After she sewed it, she put on the shoes, put on the coat, and everything looked as if it had not been assembled from shreds. This dress is beautiful and warm. When the clothes were finished and the leaf fall began. The river is frozen over. Then the snow fell. She went to look for her sister. She found her in the middle of the road. Her sister was cold from the cold. Cold without clothes. One came to her relatives.
